note: Row-count assertions for the derived text surface and the indexed attribute bag — the two behaviours the k8s-logs-line schema adds. It runs against logs.k8s_logs_v2, a frozen copy of logs.k8s_logs (967,912 rows, ts < 2026-08-19 22:19:00) carrying the STORED `line` column and the widened index group (msg, line, kv). Point it at logs.k8s_logs once the migration in round4-live-migration.sql has run there. Baselines are relative, so the suite stays valid as the table grows.

cases.name: a bare word reaches text the pipeline moved into the bag
cases.note: The whole point of the derived surface. `err=RemoteStopped` is parsed out of the message into the kv bag, so before `line` existed a bare RemoteStopped matched nothing at all: measured 0 through the index and 0 for msg LIKE '%RemoteStopped%', against 605 for line LIKE '%RemoteStopped%'.

cases.name: the message column keeps its narrow scope
cases.note: The negative control for the case above, and the reason one index spans both columns rather than the derived column replacing msg. If this is ever nonzero, `msg:` has silently widened to the reconstructed line and a user asking about the message text is being answered about the attributes too.

cases.name: a bare word and a message term compose in one search function
cases.note: Two columns of one index inside a single query() call. Two separate indexes cannot be mixed — measured, a table with idx_line(line) and idx_line2(line2) answers each alone and fails [1065] for a query naming both — so this case failing is the signal that the columns have drifted apart into different indexes.

cases.name: a bag key is searched through the index
cases.note: An inverted index covers a VARIANT column by JSON path, so kv['err'] is reachable as kv.err with no per-key DDL. Measured 507, exactly what the equality alone returns.

cases.name: an indexed bag key is still exact
cases.note: The index is tokenised and stemmed and therefore strictly wider than the equality it accelerates: query('kv.request:command') alone returns 501 rows whose value is `batch_commands`, none of which equals `command`. The compiler keeps the equality as a residual beside the index clause, so this must stay zero. If it ever returns 501, the residual has been dropped and every bag-key search has silently become a stemmed substring match.

cases.name: a bag key narrows the bare word
cases.note: The bare word finds the value anywhere in the reconstructed line; the field-scoped form insists it is that key's value. 507 against 605 when measured — the 98 others carry the token in a different key or in the message.

cases.name: a bag key search still finds nothing for an absent value
a numeric bound on a bag key is compared as a number, not as text
cases.note: Every value of kv['term'] on this table is between 19 and 175, so a numeric `>= 9` is all 33,300 rows that hold the key and the assertion is an identity. Read as text it is 339, because '10' sorts before '9'. This case replaced a `partitions` one that could not fail: `> x` and `[0 TO x]` are complementary halves of the key's rows under EITHER comparison, so the partition identity held at 32,929 + 371 and again at 30,584 + 2,716, and the case passed for both readings. Reverting the comparison to text must break this one.

cases.name: a numeric bound the table cannot satisfy returns nothing
cases.note: The other half of the case above and the more alarming one. The minimum value of kv['term'] here is 19, so nothing is below 9. Compared as text this returns 32,961 rows — a third of the key's rows invented out of a bound the table cannot satisfy, with no error. One-sided by construction, so it is paired with the identity above: a compile that returns 0 for everything passes this and fails that.

cases.name: a numeric bound silently excludes values that are not numbers
cases.note: This case asserts a KNOWN LIMITATION rather than a fix, which is why it is here. All 1,945 values of kv['duration'] are Go durations — `47.823614ms`, `39.422927ms` — so TRY_CAST yields NULL for 1,943 of them and `duration:>100` returns 0. The compiler warns, and the warning is the whole mitigation. If this case ever stops holding, the cast semantics changed and the warning text needs rechecking. Under the old hard cast this statement was [1006] invalid float literal rather than an answer at all.

cases.name: a numeric bound survives a bag key that is not all numbers
cases.note: 1,243 of store_id's 40,516 rows hold a `Some(25)`-style debug rendering. Compiled as a cast this is not a wrong answer but a dead query: `kv['store_id']::VARCHAR::DOUBLE > 100` is [1006] invalid float literal, and one such value anywhere in the table is enough — so reverting the cast makes this case error rather than pass. TRY_CAST yields NULL for those rows and returns the 39,140 that are numbers, so this must be nonzero and strictly below the count that merely have the key. The decomposition: 40,516 hold the key, 39,273 cast, 39,140 of those exceed 100 and 133 do not, and 40,516 - 39,273 = 1,243 do not cast. The 1,243 is the silently-excluded set the compiler now warns about.

cases.name: a bag key that cannot be spelled in the query language still works
cases.note: The query() field name has no quoting, so a key with a space in it cannot be addressed there. Such a key has to stay on the equality path rather than be silently mangled into `kv.msg type:...`, which would change where the statement's one search function is spent and probably not parse.

cases.name: an exclusion partitions the table once the bag is indexed
cases.note: 923,273 + 44,639 = 967,912 exactly. This replaced a bare `nonzero` on the same query, which asserted nothing: the failure mode it was named for — the residual leaking so the exclusion becomes NOT query(...) — also returns 923,273 for this key, because on `container` the index and the equality happen to agree.

cases.name: an exclusion on a bag key does not leak the index clause
cases.note: The discriminating version of the case above, on the one key where the index and the equality disagree. Nothing equals `command`, so excluding it must leave the whole table: 967,912. If the residual leaked under NOT and the exclusion compiled to NOT query('kv.request:command') instead, this returns 339,548 — not 967,411, because a bare NOT around a search function is pruned rather than complemented, which is the older defect this project already fixed for the text column. Either way it is a quarter of the table missing and this case sees it.

cases.name: a stopword bag value skips the index
cases.note: kv['standalone'] = 'No' on exactly one row in this window, and `No` is one of the 33 words the analyzer deletes — so query('kv.standalone:No') is 0 while the equality is 1. The index clause must not be added beside the equality here, or the AND inherits the emptiness and a row that exists returns nothing. This is the only naturally occurring all-stopword bag value in the table; the multi-token form (`verb:"to be"`, which the first version of the guard let through) is not reachable here and is covered by TestStopwordBagValueSkipsIndex, measured on a purpose-built probe.

cases.name: a declared column is not read from the attribute bag
cases.note: The general form of a defect that reached production. A real column the descriptor does not declare is not merely missing: with a bag configured, every query naming it is routed into the bag, where it matches nothing, and the advisory says the name "is not a column" — which is false. Measured on this table, `source_file IS NOT NULL AND source_file <> ''` is 795,924 rows while `kv['source_file'] IS NOT NULL` is 0, so this case returns 795,924 while declared and 0 the moment the declaration is dropped. It caught `raw` on the live table: 5,112 rows in the column, 0 under the bag key. The regression guard for the specific column is TestPresetDeclaresEveryLiveColumn, which compares the shipped presets against a captured table shape.

cases.name: a disjunction mixing full text with a field filter keeps both branches
cases.note: The defect was worse than a typo hazard. A search function inside a disjunction makes the scan visit only the blocks the index says contain matches, and the other branch is evaluated only in those blocks — so what is lost is the other branch's rows in the blocks the text term never touched. On this 5-block copy, with level=ERROR spread over all five: `peer`/`snapshot` touch 5 blocks and lose nothing, `rejections` touches 4 and loses 20.0%, `RemoteStopped` touches 4 and loses 26.2%. So this case is discriminating: the old shape answers 253,587 where the union is 343,695, which is BELOW the baseline and fails `gt`. Compiled as a row-key semi-join it is exact.

cases.name: a disjunction whose full-text branch matches nothing keeps the other branch
cases.note: The limit of the same mechanism: zero matches means zero blocks visited, so the other branch is lost entirely. Measured on this table the old shape returns 0 against a truth of 343,090, and on the live table `query(...) OR 1=1` returns 0 of 1,063,259 — the whole table discarded because one branch matched nothing. Branch order is irrelevant. Keyed on the row the answer is exactly the other branch, so this must equal the field filter alone.

cases.name: a three-branch disjunction loses no branch
cases.note: The loss is not limited to a pair. Measured live, `query(NO-MATCH) OR level=ERROR OR level=WARN` returned 0 against a truth of 463,701 — two branches gone — because pruning is a property of the scan, not of an operand pair. On this table the old shape answers 0 against 400,021.

cases.name: an excluded term ORed with a field filter still returns everything it should
cases.note: This shape was ALREADY correct before the fix, and it is why the fix looks the way it does: a negated branch compiles to an anti-join, so its search function already sat inside a subquery and pruned only there. Measured live it returns 1,063,259, the whole table, correctly. It is asserted here as a regression guard rather than as a discriminator — an earlier attempt at this change routed negated branches into the new semi-join and broke exactly this case.

cases.name: a full-text term ANDed with a field filter is unchanged
cases.note: The AND path is genuinely correct rather than accidentally so — `query(NO-MATCH) AND level=ERROR` is 0 and 0 is the truth, because pruning the scan to nothing is the right answer for a conjunction. It keeps a bare query() and no subquery. A regression guard, so the disjunction fix does not spread to the conjunction where it would cost a needless second scan.

cases.name: excluding a term is exact, not merely close
cases.note: An exactness assertion, and an honest note about what it does NOT discriminate. `partitions` demands that the excluded and included halves add up to the table exactly. That holds under BOTH the old text-keyed anti-join and the new row-keyed one, and the reason is structural: the anti-join keys on the column it searched, and two rows with identical text match or miss the index together, so expanding the match set by shared text is idempotent — measured, `query('msg:snapshot')` is 17,661 rows and `msg IN (SELECT msg WHERE query('msg:snapshot'))` is also 17,661. Verified across 14 term/preset combinations on a 1,063,259-row table, every one identical. So the negation was already exact; the row key is a simplification there (no COALESCE) and insurance against the keying and the search ever diverging, which is the one arrangement that IS wrong: keying on msg while searching line gives 1,035,332 against a truth of 1,036,932.

cases.name: a full-text term inside a conjunction inside a disjunction keeps both branches
cases.note: The shape the previous round missed. A conjunction collapses its full-text child into ordinary SQL, so by the time the surrounding disjunction is assembled nothing can see that a search function is inside that branch - and it prunes the scan for the whole predicate exactly as a bare one would. Measured on this table the old form returns 253,002 where the truth is 343,110, losing 90,108 rows (26.3%); on the live table `level:WARN OR (level:ERROR RemoteStopped)` returned 27,502 of a true 60,727, losing 54.7%. `RemoteStopped` is deliberately the term here: it touches 4 of this table's 5 blocks, so it misses one. A common term like `region` touches all five and would make this case pass under the defect, proving nothing. The fix hoists the whole branch into a row-key subquery, giving 343,110 = 343,090 + 20.

cases.name: two branches each combining full text with a filter both survive
cases.note: This used to be a compile error - two search functions in one statement, which the engine allows only one of. Each branch now goes into its own subquery, which is its own scan, so it compiles and is exact: 53,212 = 585 + 52,627 with no overlap, and on the live table the equivalent is 379,169 = 375,692 + 3,477. So the fix removes a refusal as well as a wrong answer. Under the old compiler this case fails by failing to compile at all.

cases.name: a bare word still finds nothing that is not there
cases.note: Control. The derived column concatenates two things, so a bug in the expression would show up as a term matching more than it should, not less.
